description:
Fix the confirmed repair bug exposed by the post-integration acceptance suite: when a default-origin rule's derived assertion is stale, `jit validate --fix` must restore the config-derived assertion without removing authored `rules.toml` bytes such as the file header or editable policy fields.

## Background

The acceptance work for `b1621508` reproduces the same failure on JSON and InMemory backends. The repair currently drops an authored first-line header and leaves the stale default-origin assertion unchanged. The approved ownership matrix in `dev/active/cdc840ad-plan.md` §2/D7 requires authored rule content to be preserved while generated default-rule fragments are repaired from declared configuration.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: On both JSON and InMemory backends, repairing a stale default-origin assertion restores the exact assertion derived from declared configuration while preserving the authored `rules.toml` header, comments, ordering, and editable policy fields byte-for-byte.
- [hard] REQ-02: The correction uses the existing rules-document span ownership and repository-state transaction path; it adds no alternate renderer, whole-file fallback rewrite, compatibility seam, or second publisher.
- [hard] REQ-03: Focused regressions prove the repair and a second fix is a no-op; ambiguous ownership remains non-repairable and zero-write.

## Constraints

- Keep the change narrow to the existing rules materializer/repair path and its cohesive tests.
- Preserve all authored rule policy unconditionally; filename or default-origin convention alone never authorizes a whole-file rewrite.
- Do not broaden into the remaining acceptance matrix owned by `b1621508`.
title: Preserve authored rules while repairing derived assertions
